title: Design problem: sorting cans with a magnet
subject: Physics

sources.title: NGSS 3-PS2-4: Define a simple design problem that can be solved by applying scientific ideas about magnets
Bunting: Recovering steel and aluminum cans with magnetic separators

note.text: At a recycling center, a belt carries a jumble of cans. The design problem: separate steel cans from aluminum ones.
note.remember: A design problem says what needs to be solved.

steps.title: Rollers
steps.instruction: Draw the rollers at each end.

note.text: The rollers turn and keep the belt moving, so the cans pass under the magnet one after another.

steps.title: Magnet
steps.instruction: Trace the big magnet hanging above the belt.

note.text: Magnets attract objects made of iron or steel, even without touching them.

steps.title: Steel cans
steps.instruction: Trace the steel can on the belt and the one being lifted.

note.text: Steel contains iron, so the magnet pulls steel cans up off the belt.
Aluminum isn't attracted to magnets, so aluminum cans stay on the belt and ride on to their own bin.

steps.title: Arrows
steps.instruction: Draw the arrows: one lifting the steel can, one moving the aluminum on.

note.text: One simple idea, that magnets attract steel but not aluminum, solves the sorting problem.

steps.title: Explain
steps.question: Why does the aluminum can stay on the belt?

options.feedback: Right. Only iron and steel (and a few other metals) are pulled by the magnet.
Aluminum cans are light. They stay because magnets don't attract aluminum.
The magnet is working: it's lifting the steel can.
Nothing holds it down. The magnet just doesn't attract aluminum.

steps.title: Define a problem
steps.question: Which of these problems could you solve with a magnet?

options.text: Picking up spilled steel paper clips from the floor
options.feedback: Yes. Steel clips are attracted to a magnet, so you can sweep it over the floor and lift them up.
Neither paper nor plastic is attracted to magnets.
Ordinary sand isn't attracted to magnets.
Glass isn't attracted to magnets, whatever its color.
